idiom_name: ERB in the standard library, wrapped by Rails ActionView
implementation_notes: ERB ships with Ruby: ERB.new(File.read('orders.html.erb'), trim_mode: '-').result(binding) evaluates <%= %> markers against a binding, which is the template-plus-model mechanism in the standard library; what the classic structure adds is an object that owns both the binding and the escaping helper, and Rails' ActionView is exactly that (layouts, partials, view helpers and ActiveSupport::SafeBuffer escaping). Production code therefore uses ActionView - or Haml/Slim as alternative syntaxes over the same idea - while raw ERB remains the tool for scripts and generated text; Rails eagerly loads (compiles) templates when config.eager_load is on, so errors surface before the first request.
code_sketch:
require 'erb'
require 'erb/util'

class OrderPage
  def initialize(rows) = @rows = rows
  def render = ERB.new(TEMPLATE, trim_mode: '-').result(binding)
  def h(text) = ERB::Util.html_escape(text)   # every dynamic value goes through this
end

puts OrderPage.new(rows).render
pitfalls: result(binding) evaluates template code in a real Ruby scope and raw ERB escapes nothing: each <%= %> of user data must call ERB::Util.html_escape (ActionView's <%= auto-escapes, raw/html_safe does not).
The binding exposes the caller's locals and ivars to the template, so a template can read or mutate state it was never given; keep the binding object's public surface small.
Templates are compiled on first use unless the app precompiles or eager-loads them, so a typo surfaces on the request path.
